title: County of Vermandois
capsule: The County of Vermandois was a Carolingian-era lordship in Picardy, centered on Saint-Quentin and Péronne, whose comital dynasty claimed descent directly from Charlemagne through Bernard of Italy. The county reached its height under Herbert II (died 943), who held the Carolingian king Charles the Simple prisoner at Péronne (923–929) and wielded enormous influence over the French kingdom. The male Herbertian line died out in 1080, after which Vermandois passed through marriage to the counts of Flanders, and Philip II of France absorbed it into the royal domain by 1213 following the County of Flanders succession dispute.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political history is well attested in Carolingian annals and chronicles; territorial boundaries are broadly known but shift with sub-enfeoffments.
